problems.problem: You can't send until you've confirmed your email. That puts a 3-screen, 3-action detour in the middle of the first send: open the email, press Confirm email, then 'Go to Sign&Grow'. The confirm link opens a new tab, so the tab you signed up in still shows the yellow banner until you reload it. The confirmation email is 135 words and explains browsers and passwords.

The envelope page right after the first send is crowded: 37 choices, 436 words, 1.9 screenfuls. The header has Preview PDF, Download evidence pack, Clone, Save as template and Void. The person's card has 6 more buttons (Nudge, Copy link, Show QR code, Share on WhatsApp, Share by text message, Correct). These repeat 'Send reminder' and 'Edit envelope' a few lines above. A comment box with a 'Who can read it' select is always open. The audit trail shows the IP 127.0.0.1 and hash ids. The 'Sent' toast covers the person's action buttons, and the sidebar still says 0 sheets saved.

The helper fails on the most likely question. 'I cannot sign this today. What can I do?' gets 'I could not find that in our help pages, and I would rather not guess' and is sent to a person. Yet 'Finish later' and 'Ask Rosa M. Gardener for more time' are both on the same page.

On the consent screen, where someone who can't sign now actually is, Other actions has no 'Finish later'. It only appears after they agree and press Continue. The sheet lists 8 options, each with a description, about 97 words. The deadline is shown in UTC ('20 March 2027 at 22:33 UTC') instead of the signer's own time.

The landing page is 7.3 screenfuls, 2,403 words and 42 choices. The top bar has 9 links, including 'Check an email', 'Verify a document', 'API', and both 'Ask for help' and 'Help'. Below come 'Nine things that go wrong elsewhere', a comparison table and a long 'The rules' list. On a new server the live counters read '0.0005 trees' and 'US$0'.

The app home has 4 buttons that start nearly the same thing: the yellow 'New envelope', 'Send for signature', 'Send your first envelope' and 'Sign a document yourself'. The sidebar has 14 entries with jargon (Envelopes, Bulk send, PowerForms, Click-to-agree, Our impact), plus both 'Ask for help' and 'Help'. While loading, the Paper saved card shows '...' and 'sheets, or ... of a tree'.

Editor step 1 starts with no recipient row, so you must press 'Add recipient' first. Each row then adds a 6-option role select ('Needs to sign' through 'Is a witness'), an 'I will send the link myself' checkbox and 'More'. The email box is too narrow and cuts off the start of the address ('da-mwpk1zew@example.org').

Step 1 asks first-time senders for things they don't need: 'Remind every (days, 0 for never)', 'Expires after (days)' set to 120, and a date format select with a 60-word note about time zones and UTC. Reminders are asked again on step 3 with a different control (a select), so the same choice appears twice.

The document name and email subject come from the file name. You get 'Please sign: planting-partnership' (lowercase, with a hyphen), and it shows up in the invitation email, the signer's title bar, every list and the downloaded file name ('Please sign_ planting-partnership.pdf').

Placing one signature means facing 17 field types (including Strike out, Stamp, Note, Attachment), 'Find fields for me' with '{{signature}} tags' jargon, and keyboard and shortcut instructions. Selecting the field opens a panel with 'Only show when...' logic, Width and Height in %, a screen-reader label note and 'Copy to every page'. That is 37 choices on one screen.

On a phone the consent screen is 2.2 screenfuls. About 170 words of legal and practical text sit before the checkbox, and the 'Sent by / Email / Account' box names the sender twice ('Rosa Gardener's workspace').

'Next' only scrolls to the signature, so a second tap on the field is needed to open the dialog. The 'Sign here' bubble covers the 'Date:' label. Six controls (Document/Text view, 100/150/200%, Download, Questions and comments) fill about 40% of the first phone screen before the document starts.

The completed envelope page has 3 overlapping ways to get the file (View signed PDF, Download with certificate, Download evidence pack) next to Clone, Save as template and Delete. Six header buttons squeeze the title into 3 lines. The audit trail, with IPs, hashes and 'Time zone reported' rows, takes most of the page. A Download button already exists on each completed row in the list, but nothing on Home points there.

The Help dialog opens with two paragraphs of disclaimers and a bold warning before the question box. 'Talk to a person' then asks for name and email again, although the signing page already knows both (only the question carries over).
'Adopt your signature' / 'Adopt and sign' is borrowed jargon. 'Check before you finish' then adds a second confirmation dialog and tap for a single signature that's already on the page.

The invitation email is 204 words for 'please sign'. Under the button sit a security-code panel, 'Report this email', a fallback link, 'Page will not open where you are?', 'Do not forward' and a help link. The closing date is in UTC.
The review step, done screen and envelope page all quote tiny impact figures ('0.01 kg of CO2e', '0.0002 of a tree', '20 litres of water'). They read as noise rather than reward.

The flow itself is good (5 actions). But each template row has 6 actions (Use, Send to a list, Edit, Move, Who can use this, Delete), the page intro is about permissions, and the Use dialog adds a 4-line reminder paragraph. After sending, the back link says 'Envelopes' rather than 'Templates', and there's no 'Sent' banner like after flow (a).

Changing the name is easy (3 actions). The Profile tab, though, mixes name, email change, signature, password, two-step login (with developer text: 'API keys are not affected...') and a signed-in list with long explanations, behind 8 tabs. The 'Saved' toast lands mid-page over the password field.

Other Settings tabs carry walls of text: the Plan tab has 16 rule bullets (about 800 words) and the Your data tab has two long kept/deleted lists before 'Close my account'. Sending defaults (reminders, deadline, date format) sit under 'Account' while the editor asks for the same things on every envelope.

Completed documents: one Download (signed PDF with its signing record); evidence pack becomes 'Full record for disputes' in More; at most two header buttons so the title stays on one line.
Signing page: Next jumps to the field and opens it; the 'Sign here' bubble never covers a label; zoom, view, download and comments move into the toolbar's More.
Consent screen: 120 words or fewer before the tick, sender named once, Other actions offers Finish later already, at most 6 options without descriptions, deadline in the signer's own time.
Rename 'Adopt your signature' and 'Adopt and sign' to 'Your signature' and 'Sign'; skip 'Check before you finish' when nothing needs attention.
Help: question box first with one line of caution; built-in answers cover 'I cannot sign today' with Finish later and Ask for more time buttons; 'Talk to a person' carries the known name and email.
Invitation email: 80 words or fewer above the button, the code, report and fallback links in a short footer, dates in the person's own time.
No impact figure under 1 tree anywhere; signers see '10 mangroves will be planted when you finish' only for paid signatures.
Landing page: 4 top links, at most 3 phone screenfuls and 800 words, comparison and rules moved to /pricing and /help, live counters hidden until at least 1 tree.

Templates: Use on each row and the other five actions in the row's More; intro without permissions text; Use dialog without the reminder paragraph; after sending the back link says Templates and a Sent banner shows.

Settings: split Profile into Profile and Sign-in and security; 'Saved' next to the button that saved; Plan rules behind 'How signatures work'; Your data lists behind 'What is kept'; sending defaults move from Account to a new Sending section.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Login, 2.7 vs ds-sso-oidc and gov-G08
corrections.problem: 2.7 says 'Login: email first'. That turns sign-in into two screens for every user (email, Continue, then password). Meanwhile ds-sso-oidc says 'the login page is unchanged'. Sign-in is not one of the measured flows, so the budget would never catch it.
corrections.fix: Keep email and password on one screen. When the typed address belongs to a claimed domain, the password box is replaced in place by 'Continue with <Org> sign-in' as the person leaves the email box. Add flow g-sign-in (landing > Sign in > Home) to tests/ux/flows.cjs, with today's numbers as its ceiling.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Quick win 2, signing your own document
corrections.problem: Quick win 2 removes 'Sign a document yourself'. Today that is /app/envelopes/new?self=1, which prefills you as the signer. After the change, self-signing becomes: upload, Add me, step 2, step 3, Send, then find the signing page. That is a common job made longer, and no flow measures it.
corrections.fix: When the only person is the sender, step 3's main button reads 'Sign now' and opens the signing page in the same tab, with no invitation email. Add flow h-sign-myself, with today's ?self=1 path as its ceiling.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Idle check on the signing page (2.6, ds-sec-policy)
corrections.problem: 2.6 lists 'Still there? Continue' after 30 idle minutes with no condition. It is a dialog the signer did not open, which breaks P9. It interrupts someone reading a long lease, and it contradicts ds-sec-policy's default of idle sign-out off.
corrections.fix: Signing page: only when the account set 'Sign out after [ ] minutes', and never as a timed popup. On the first action after the limit, check the link again in place, keep every answer, and show one line: 'You were away for a while, so we checked the link again.' Accounts with the rule off get nothing.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Impact lines for signers (impact, 2.6 item 3)
corrections.problem: A paying signer gets three tree moments: a line at the top of the consent screen, one next to Finish, and the Done celebration. The consent screen is the legal moment (gov-G01 keeps trees out of the record), and b-sign-phone's word target is 450. 'Rosa pays, not you' brings money onto a signer screen, which P7 forbids.
corrections.fix: One tree line per signer, next to Finish ('10 mangroves will be planted when you finish.'), plus the Done celebration. Nothing on the consent screen. Move 'Rosa pays, not you' into Help's built-in answer to 'Do I have to pay anything?'.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Things always visible on the a-send-first path with zero setup
corrections.problem: Several additions are 'Available' by default, so each one adds choices to a-send-first while its ceiling still equals the baseline: 'Pages' on each file row, 'Add me', 'See what they see' next to every person, and 'Draft a message' (step 3 shows it whenever the AI helper switch is on, which is on by default). The charter never costs these out.
corrections.fix: (1) 'Draft a message' only when a model is configured and the switch is on (P3), not on the switch alone. (2) Replace one 'See what they see' per person with one link above Who gets it, 'See what each person sees', which opens the preview with a person switch in its band. (3) In section 3, list every always-visible addition with its choice cost, and require the quick win for that screen to merge first.

corrections.about: [untestable] Budget only measures zero setup (section 3, P1)
corrections.problem: Real customers will have features switched on: 2 languages, text or WhatsApp, an ID provider, AI, details, deletion schedules, 2 or more members. In that state every 'only when set up' item lands at once in the person's More, step 3 More options and the envelope page More, and nothing measures it. 'Keep it as small as the feature allows' cannot be tested. P8's government comparison is not run either.
corrections.fix: Add two profiles to flows.cjs. 'Everything set up' fakes every operator service and turns on 2 languages, AI, details, a deletion schedule and 2 members. 'Government' sets DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=government. Record each profile's first run as its own ceiling. Then write the rule as numbers: a switched-on check the sender chose may add at most 1 screen and 60 words to a flow; any other switched-on feature may add at most 1 action and 0 screens.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Order of quick wins and features (section 7)
corrections.problem: Section 7 says the quick wins are only 'worth doing before' the features. If feature batches land first, they spend the slack (193 choices, 3751 words) before any ceiling is lowered.
corrections.fix: Make it a rule: no batch changes a core screen until that screen's quick win has merged and its new numbers are written into section 3 as ceilings.

corrections.about: [trip] Role list in the person's More (2.3, ds-recipient-types, ds-notary)
corrections.problem: Role grows from 6 to 10 options in one select, and the baseline already flagged 6 as too many. 'Signs in person' describes how someone signs, not a role. 'Needs to view' next to 'Gets a copy' is unclear. Notary is listed in 2.3 without 'only when set up'.
corrections.fix: Lead with 5 options: Needs to sign, Needs to approve, Gets a copy, Must open it (today 'Needs to view', the same words as ds-supplements), Is a witness. Move 'Signs in person' to How they sign ('In person, with me'). After a divider at the end: Can change the document, Chooses who comes next, and Notary (only when set up). Testable cap: at most 8 options with everything set up.

corrections.about: [trip] Size of the person's More (2.3 items 1 to 7)
corrections.problem: One More holds 7 groups. A sender who opens it only to choose 'Gets a copy' wades through language, delivery, checks, signing methods, conditions, waits and the note.
corrections.fix: Show each group as one line with its current value ('How they get it: Email') that opens a small picker. Do not list a group that has only one possible value. With zero setup that leaves Role, How they get it, Check who signs and Private note. 'Wait before this person' appears only with signing order on. Testable cap: at most 6 lines inside any item's More with zero setup, at most 8 with everything set up. The inventory opens every More to check.

corrections.about: [contradiction] Only when... in step 1 (ds-routing-if)
corrections.problem: 'Only when Amount is more than 1000' is set in the person's More on step 1, but fields are placed on step 2. On a new document there is nothing to pick.
corrections.fix: List 'Only when...' in the person's More only once the document has a field it can test: after returning from step 2, or in a template. Otherwise leave it out. Show any set condition as one line under that person in step 3's Who gets it.

corrections.about: [sprawl] Step 3 More options (2.3, ds-switches)
corrections.problem: Step 3's More options holds about 13 items: Send later, reminders, deadline, date format, pass it on, questions and comments, words across copies, ways to make a signature (per ds-switches), each person sees only theirs, sign in to sign, summary, payment, send for a colleague. That is a settings page inside the send flow.
corrections.fix: Keep only what changes from one send to the next: Send later, Reminders, Deadline, 'Each person sees only their files' (2 or more files), Ask for a payment (when set up), Plain summary for signers (when allowed), Send for <name> (when shared). Date format, pass it on, questions and comments, ways to make a signature and words across pages stay as account defaults in Settings > Sending and as template settings, never per send. Cap: 7 items with everything set up.

corrections.about: [trip] The envelope page's More (2.5)
corrections.problem: It lists 14 items. 'Delete now' and 'Delete' sit side by side. 'Keep it', 'Hold' and 'Delete now' would show even with deletion schedules off, which breaks P3. Preview and Download (when not main) do nearly the same thing.
corrections.fix: One Delete. When a schedule applies, its dialog gives the scheduled date and offers 'Keep it' instead. Show 'Keep it' and 'Hold' only when a deletion schedule is on, and Hold only to admins. Fold Preview and Download into 'Open the PDF' when the document is not completed. Cap: 9 items in the busiest state.

corrections.about: [trip] Remind twice on the envelope page (2.5)
corrections.problem: The main button 'Send a reminder' and each person's More 'Remind' sit on the same page. That is two controls for one job, and P12's own test fails.
corrections.fix: The main button names who it reminds ('Remind Ana Silva'). A per-person Remind appears only when 2 or more people are waiting at the same time.

corrections.about: [jargon] WhatsApp and Text mean two opposite things (2.5 vs ds-channels)
corrections.problem: In the editor, How they get it: WhatsApp means 'we send it'. On the envelope page, the person's More: WhatsApp means 'share it from your own phone'. Same word, opposite meaning, both on the sender's daily path.
corrections.fix: On the envelope page, put Copy link, QR code, WhatsApp and Text under one entry, 'Share the link yourself', shown open for people set to 'I will send the link myself'. A bare 'WhatsApp' anywhere else always means we send it.

corrections.about: [untestable] Other actions cap (2.6)
corrections.problem: 'At most 6 at a time, only those that apply' covers 6 standard and 5 situational entries, with no order and no rule for which ones drop. Two engineers will build two different menus.
corrections.fix: Write a fixed order: 1 Finish later, 2 Ask for more time, 3 Pass to someone else (or Hand back to <group>), 4 Questions and comments, 5 Sign on paper instead (when allowed), 6 Decline, always last. Witnesses get their own list: I was not there, Questions and comments, Help. Move 'Stop reminder emails' into the reminder email's footer and the Finish later message. Drop 'Change my signature', because tapping a placed signature already does it. The list then never needs more than 6.

corrections.about: [contradiction] Help disappears when AI is off (gov-G20, gov-G01)
corrections.problem: gov-G20's 'Never: a help button when the switch is off' means an admin who turns off the AI helper also removes Help, the built-in answers and 'Talk to a person' for everyone they send to. The chat note says built-in answers are the fallback.
corrections.fix: Switch off means built-in answers only. The Help entry and 'Talk to a person' always stay. Reword gov-G20's Never to: 'a model answer when the switch is off, a hosted model in sovereign mode.'

corrections.about: [jargon] Model line on signer screens (gov-G20)
corrections.problem: 'Answers come from <model> on <host>' at the foot of Help shows a model name and a host name on the signing page and public pages. P6 forbids technical names on signer screens.
corrections.fix: On signer screens and public pages, show only 'Answers are written by AI and can be wrong. Do not type passwords or card numbers.' Show the model line only in the app's Help (senders and admins) and on /security.

corrections.about: [trip] Plain summary hidden in the toolbar (ds-ai-assist)
corrections.problem: The sender switched on a plain summary for signers, but signers only find it under the toolbar's More, which almost nobody opens. The feature costs work and helps no one.
corrections.fix: When the sender switched it on, show one link above the document, in the same place as 'Also for you': 'Summary (written by AI, check it)'. Keep it out of the toolbar.

corrections.about: [contradiction] Placement on the signing page not settled (2.6 vs ds-pay-collect, ds-delegate, ds-part11, gov-G17, ds-retention)
corrections.problem: Five things are not settled. The Pay screen has no position in 2.6's order. 'Signing for Ana Silva' is not placed. Strict signing's password check is 'at Finish' in ds-part11 but 'in the signature dialog' in 2.6 item 5. gov-G17's verified badge is not in the header list, and a badge is a trust claim (P13). 'Remove names and answers' (redaction) is not placed anywhere.
corrections.fix: In 2.6: Pay comes after the last signature and before Done, never before consent. 'Signing for Ana Silva' joins the header's sender line. Strict signing asks the reason in the signature dialog and the password once at Finish. The header shows 'From acme.org (address checked)' as words, only for verified sending domains, never as a badge. Redaction becomes the second choice inside the deletion schedule card: 'At the end: Delete the files / Remove names and answers, keep the record'.

corrections.about: [contradiction] Identity before or after consent (2.6 vs ds-id-login)
corrections.problem: 2.6 puts 'Prove who you are' (screen 2) before Consent (screen 3). The ds-id-login note says 'after consent'.
corrections.fix: Choose codes, then consent, then prove who you are, and correct whichever text disagrees. This way someone who wants paper or wants to decline finds Other actions before handing over a bank login or a passport photo. The identity screen names the sender and the document in one line.

corrections.about: [longer flow] Identity and signing stack up (ds-id-login, ds-qtsp, ds-webeid, gov-G25)
corrections.problem: Smart-ID or BankID can appear under both Check who signs and How they sign. A sender can pick both and send the signer to the same provider twice. The charter also never says whether Check who signs allows more than one check.
corrections.fix: Check who signs is one choice per person. Picking a scheme under How they sign sets Check who signs to 'Done by <scheme> when they sign' and removes the separate screen. Charter rule: at most one check screen and one trip to a provider per signer.

corrections.about: [sprawl] Number of Settings sections (2.2)
corrections.problem: Today there are 8 tabs. The owner of a one-person account with zero setup would see 11, and an organisation admin with everything on would see 14. 'Sign-in and security' and 'Security' side by side leave no clue where 'two-step for everyone' or your own two-step lives.
corrections.fix: Make one Security section. Its first card, 'Your sign-in', is for everyone: password, two-step, ways to sign in, where you are signed in. Admin cards follow: sign-in rules, single sign-on, members from your directory, security record, your own encryption key. Members then see 3 or 4 sections. Add to section 5's check: an owner with zero setup sees at most 10 sections, a member at most 4.

corrections.about: [sprawl] Settings > Sending (2.2)
corrections.problem: Sending gathers about 16 controls in one section: reminders, deadline, date format, pass it on, questions, words across copies, ways to sign, paper, visibility, access code rules, the in-person question, details, saved fields, consent text, strict signing and signature level rules.
corrections.fix: Three open cards: 'New documents' (reminders, deadline, date format); 'When people sign' (pass it on, questions and comments, ways to make a signature, paper, each person sees only their files, marking pages); 'Details and saved fields'. The rare rules go behind the section's one More options: access code rules, the in-person ID question, your consent text, strict signing, signature level rules. Rule for every section: at most 4 cards open with zero setup.

corrections.about: [contradiction] Who may add identity providers (2.2 Connections vs ds-id-login)
corrections.problem: Connections is 'listed only when the operator set up at least one service'. Yet ds-id-login says admins add their own providers. On a server with no operator service, an admin has nowhere to add one.
corrections.fix: Put admin-added identity providers in Settings > Security, next to single sign-on, using the same OpenID Connect form. Connections stays operator-gated and lists only operator services.

corrections.about: [untestable] P5 vs Settings cards and the sidebar
corrections.problem: 'Each card saves on its own with its button' puts several filled buttons on one Settings page. The sidebar's yellow 'Send a document' is also a primary button on every app page. P5's test ('exactly one') fails everywhere.
corrections.fix: Switches and selects save as soon as they change, with 'Saved' next to them. Text cards get a secondary Save. P5 counts only the page body and dialogs. Give the sidebar start button its own class and leave it out of the count.

corrections.about: [untestable] P4 vs the charter's own screens
corrections.problem: The envelope page has 5 folded sections, step 3 has '2 more things to check', step 2 has 'More fields', and Settings cards have their own More options. P4 says nothing else expands options, so its test fails on screens the charter itself designs. 'Remembered closed' can be read two ways.
corrections.fix: Define three kinds, each with a data attribute: data-more='screen' (at most 1 per screen), data-more='item' (at most 1 per item: person, file, field, card, row) and data-fold (content sections, closed by default, allowed). Count them by attribute. Replace 'remembered closed' with 'closed every time the screen opens'. The sidebar's More group is the exception: it opens by itself on a page inside it and remembers being open for that person, so daily Send to many users do not pay an extra click.

corrections.about: [untestable] P3 grep test
corrections.problem: Grepping rendered pages for words like Language, Pages, Details, Hold, Format or Pay gives false hits, so the test is not mechanical.
corrections.fix: Every gated element carries data-feature='<key>'. With zero setup, the inventory may contain no data-feature element whose key is marked gated. Add one column to section 6 with each feature's gated or always-on status.

corrections.about: [untestable] P12 and P13 tests
corrections.problem: 'No two controls with the same job' is a judgement, not a check. P13 has no test at all.
corrections.fix: P12: a list of labels allowed at most once per screen (Download, Help, Delete, Remind, Send, Questions and comments, Language), checked by the inventory script. P13: scan public and signer pages for certified, qualified, compliant, accredited, ISO, SOC 2, HIPAA and eIDAS. Every hit must match a registry entry marked held, or sit in a sentence saying it is not held.

corrections.about: [untestable] Consent word cap with the account's own text (P7, ds-consent-own)
corrections.problem: Account text of 60 words or fewer is shown inline. Together with our sentence and any line about the document, that can push the consent screen past 120 words. P6's 'sender's daily path' is also undefined.
corrections.fix: The 120-word cap holds with every option on. Show the account's text inline only while the total stays at or under 120; otherwise put it behind 'Read <Org>'s terms'. Define the daily path as: sidebar, Home, Documents, editor steps 1 to 3, the envelope page, Templates and emails to senders.

corrections.about: [untestable] ds-switches 'a line telling the signer why'
corrections.problem: 'A hidden option without a line telling the signer why it is missing' adds explanations of features the sender did not use, which P7 forbids. It also does not say where the line goes.
corrections.fix: The explanation lives only in Help's built-in answer (for example 'How do I pass this to someone?' gets 'Rosa turned that off for this document. Use Questions and comments to ask her.'). Nothing is added to Other actions.

corrections.about: [default] Language order (ds-lang-core, ds-lang-signing)
corrections.problem: Today chooseLocale in src/lib/i18n.ts picks the sender's choice, then the browser, then English. If the account default is saved as the sender's choice, an English reader always gets French from a French account. If it is not, the email (sent before any browser is known) can be in one language and the page in another. Also, ds-lang-core's first sight shows the admin a select, while its Never forbids a select with one option.
corrections.fix: Decide one language per person at send: the person's choice, else the account default, else English. Use it for the email, texts and page alike. The header menu switches it and remembers the switch for that link. Write this order into ds-lang-signing. The Settings select stays hidden until a second language ships.

corrections.about: [default] Key dates switches on with AI reading (ds-ai-repo)
corrections.problem: An admin who turns on 'Let the AI read document text' to get field suggestions also sends every completed contract to the AI and adds a new sidebar entry, without being told.
corrections.fix: The AI card says in one line what the switch is used for. Key dates gets its own switch. It reads only documents completed after it was turned on, unless the admin presses 'Look through older documents'.

corrections.about: [default] Deletion emails and the word Closed (ds-retention, gov-G11)
corrections.problem: An email per document 14 days before deletion will flood busy senders. 'Delete closed documents after [ ] days' clashes with the Documents tab 'Closed' (declined, expired, cancelled), so an admin cannot tell whether signed contracts are included.
corrections.fix: Send one weekly email per sender, listing what will be deleted in the next 14 days, with Keep it on each row. The card says two lines: 'Delete completed documents after [ ] days' and 'Delete cancelled, declined and expired ones after [ ] days'. Rename the tab to 'Stopped' and use that word everywhere.

corrections.about: [default] Copies of every email carry live links (ds-mail-records)
corrections.problem: Archive copies of invitations contain working signing links, so anyone who can read the archive can open or sign as that person.
corrections.fix: In each copy, replace the signing link with '(link removed in this copy)'. The card's one line says so.

corrections.about: [default] A code the sender cannot read back (ds-id-small)
corrections.problem: Under 'Make one for me' plus 'Never: showing a stored code', the sender makes a code and can never see it to tell the signer.
corrections.fix: Show the code once, right after it is made or set, with Copy and the line 'Tell <name> this code yourself. We do not show it again.' 'Set a new code' is the way back.

corrections.about: [default] Paper allowed by default (ds-paper)
corrections.problem: Today's Other actions has no paper option, so 'allowed by default' is new behaviour. It gives every sender scans to review and accept, and a photographed wet signature is weaker evidence. P2 says that when unsure, the default is what the product does today.
corrections.fix: Off by default. Admins switch it on in Settings > Sending. Only then does 'paper allowed or required' appear under How they sign.

corrections.about: [default] Leaked-password check vs sovereign mode (ds-sec-policy, gov-G02)
corrections.problem: The check is on by default, but sovereign mode turns outside services off. A check that calls out either breaks sign-up or silently does nothing.
corrections.fix: In sovereign mode, use a bundled list or skip the check, and say so on /app/operator ('Leaked-password check off: no outside calls'). Never block sign-up because the check cannot run.

corrections.about: [default] Reports show everyone's sending (ds-reports)
corrections.problem: With 'all senders' as the default, a member opening Reports sees colleagues' documents.
corrections.fix: Members see their own sending, admins see all senders. Both start at the last 30 days.

corrections.about: [default] Two gates on file sources (ds-cloud-pick)
corrections.problem: 'Only for sources the operator set up and the admin allowed', with default 'Hidden', means a source the operator set up may never reach senders until an admin finds a switch.
corrections.fix: Once the operator sets a source up, it is on for every account. Admins can turn a source off in Settings > Connections > File sources.

corrections.about: [contradiction] Government default vs P8 (gov-G10)
corrections.problem: In the government profile, signature level rules are on by default, which adds 'For: <country>, <document type>' to step 3. P8's test says the editor has the same controls in the default and government profiles. A bare 'For:' is also unclear.
corrections.fix: Keep the rules off until an admin picks a default country; the government profile shows that card first in Settings > Sending. Word the line 'Signing rules: Kenya, employment contract. Change'.

corrections.about: [jargon] What 'certificate' and 'signed record' mean (gov-G01, Account, ds-qtsp, ds-eseal)
corrections.problem: Settings > Account has 'Impact lines on the certificate', while gov-G01's Never forbids 'tree words in the signed record'. On screens, 'certificate' also means the signer's certificate (ds-qtsp) and the organisation seal's certificate.
corrections.fix: Define 'signed record' once: the signed PDF and its signing record pages. Then decide whether impact lines may appear there. Rename the switch 'Trees on the signing record', and never use 'certificate' for the signing record on screens.

corrections.about: [jargon] Documents vs files (section 4 vs 2.3, ds-visibility, ds-supplements)
corrections.problem: Section 4 says an envelope is a 'document' and its parts are 'files'. The charter itself still says 'Step 1. Documents and people', 'the document row', 'Each person sees only the documents with their fields' and 'shown only with 2 or more documents'.
corrections.fix: Use 'Step 1. Files and people', 'file row', 'Each person sees only the files with their fields' and '2 or more files', and make 'To read, not sign' a per-file setting. Sweep sections 2 and 6 once.

corrections.about: [jargon] 'Seal' means three things (ds-seal, gov-G05, ds-eseal, stamp)
corrections.problem: The operator's PAdES 'Digital seal', the organisation's 'Organisation seal' (a certificate) and the 'Stamps and seals' section (stamp pictures) will be confused. A sender who reads 'Digital seal added' in History will look for it in Stamps and seals.
corrections.fix: Show the operator's seal as 'Sealed by <operator name>' in History and Checks on the file; keep 'Digital seal (PAdES)' only on the admin status line. The Organisation seal card reads 'Organisation seal (a certificate in your organisation's name, not a picture)'.

corrections.about: [jargon] Words still unclear
corrections.problem: Several labels are still unclear or not true. 'Words across unfinished copies' cannot be parsed. 'Hold (never delete)' is false, because holds end. 'Keep the identifier', 'Look', 'date formula' and 'Pair a screen' are jargon. 'Use your template Volunteer agreement?' (2.3) and 'This looks like your template... Use it?' (ds-tpl-combine) are two wordings for one line.
corrections.fix: Use: 'Mark pages until everyone has signed' (the word prefilled as 'Not signed yet'); 'Hold (kept until the hold ends)'; 'Keep their ID number on the signing record'; 'Text style'; 'Date from another date (like 30 days after signing)'; 'Connect the citizen's screen'; and one wording, 'This looks like your template Volunteer agreement. Use it?'.

corrections.about: [trip] Note lines piling up under one file (ds-convert, gov-G07, ds-tpl-combine)
corrections.problem: One upload can collect three lines: 'Converted from...', 'This file has signatures. They are kept.' and 'This looks like your template...'. Only ds-convert limits itself to one line.
corrections.fix: Global rule in 2.3: at most one note line under a file row. When more than one applies, the most urgent shows and the rest fold into '1 more note'.

corrections.about: [trip] Importing is hard to find (gov-G19)
corrections.problem: An admin moving from DocuSign looks for import on Documents, not in Settings > Records and data.
corrections.fix: For admins, the empty Documents list carries one link, 'Bring in documents from DocuSign or an export', to Settings > Records and data. It goes away once documents exist, the same pattern as ds-templates-lib.

corrections.about: [default] Home-screen line on phones (ds-phone-app)
corrections.problem: 'Shows once and is gone when dismissed' says two different things. On iPhone there is no install prompt, so the line alone cannot do the job.
corrections.fix: Show it on the first 3 visits from a phone, or until dismissed. On iPhone it opens one Help answer with the two Safari steps.

merge: Sign in to sign: per person in Check who signs, step 3 More options 'People must sign in to sign', and Settings > Sending 'Strict signing' become one setting. The account default lives in Settings > Sending, the per-person choice in Check who signs, and it is removed from step 3.
Envelope page More 'Delete now' and 'Delete' become one Delete. When a schedule applies, its dialog offers 'Keep it' instead.
Envelope page 'Emails sent' and 'History' become one History. Email lines show their delivery state inline.
Forms 'Anyone with this link can sign' and 'Fill-in form' (ds-web-forms) become one Form. The phone-first, one-question-at-a-time layout is simply how every form opens on a phone, with no choice.

Signing page 'Print, sign by hand and send a photo' (ds-paper) and 'Stop signing electronically' (ds-consent-own) become one Other actions entry, 'Sign on paper instead', with two choices inside: 'Print it and send a photo' and 'Ask <sender> to send it by post (stops signing electronically)'.
Roles 'Chooses the next person' and 'Can update addresses' (ds-recipient-types) become one role, 'Chooses who comes next' (fills in or changes the people after them).

In-person signing: the role 'Signs in person' (moved to How they sign), gov-G18 Counter, ds-id-small's host question and ds-offline-inperson become one in-person flow. Counter is its queue view for officials. There is one ID question ('Which ID did you see?') and one line saying the software cannot check an ID document.
Send to many 'Saved lists' (ds-reports) and Contacts groups become one people list kept in Contacts, used as 'any one of them signs' in the editor and 'each gets their own copy' in Send to many.
Settings 'Sign-in and security' (personal) and 'Security' (account) become one Security section: your own sign-in card first, admin cards below.
Account name and gov-G17 'Your name on emails and pages' become one name field. The white label becomes the switch 'Hide the GrowSigning name on emails and pages' next to it.
Developers 'Signing inside your site' (ds-dev-api) and 'Signing inside your portal' (gov-G17) become one card, 'Signing inside your site'.
Signing page 'Questions and comments' in the toolbar More and in Other actions: keep it in Other actions only.
Envelope page main button 'Send a reminder' and each person's 'Remind': the main button names who it reminds, and per-person Remind appears only when 2 or more people wait at once.
Envelope page 'Preview' and 'Download' (when not the main button) become one 'Open the PDF'.
The same scheme under Check who signs and How they sign (BankID, Smart-ID, gov-G25 connectors) becomes one provider trip. Choosing it to sign also counts as proving who they are.
Note lines under a file (ds-convert 'Converted from', gov-G07 'This file has signatures', ds-tpl-combine 'Use it?') become one line slot per file, the rest folded into '1 more note'.
